\chapter{Sets and Subsets as Bitmasks}
\label{ch:subsets}

\begin{tcolorbox}[enhanced, colback=white, colframe=secondaryblue, boxrule=1pt, arc=2mm]
\textbf{\large\textcolor{primaryblue}{A set of up to 64 elements is one integer: union is OR, intersection is AND, and all $2^n$ subsets are the numbers $0..2^n-1$.}}
\end{tcolorbox}

\chapterfacts{Beginner}{1500}{3}{6}{30}

\begin{plannedbox}[Planned Contents --- this chapter is not written yet]
\textbf{Part A --- Lessons}
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*, label=\textbf{A\arabic*.}, itemsep=1pt]
    \item Sets as integers: membership, insert, erase, union, intersection, difference, complement within $n$ bits
    \item Enumerating all subsets with a counter; the order and the cost $\bigO{2^n \cdot n}$
    \item Iterating over the set bits of a mask
    \item Masks of letters, positions and items as compact signatures
    \item When bitmask enumeration is enough and when it becomes DP (bitmask DP is the DP book)
\end{enumerate}

    \item \textbf{Enumerating all subsets} --- Petr and a Combination Lock {\small\color{darkgray}(CF 1097B)}, Sum of All Subset XOR Totals {\small\color{darkgray}(LeetCode 1863)}
    \item \textbf{Masks of chosen items} --- Maximum Rows Covered by Columns {\small\color{darkgray}(LeetCode 2397)}, Maximum Length of a Concatenated String with Unique Characters {\small\color{darkgray}(LeetCode 1239)}
    \item \textbf{Masks of letters and positions} --- Maximum Product of the Length of Two Palindromic Subsequences {\small\color{darkgray}(LeetCode 2002)}, Maximum Score Words Formed by Letters {\small\color{darkgray}(LeetCode 1255)}
